title: He started stroking his
subtitle: 13 operations from 4 reading(s), pooled. An operation is a NODE, and two operations are in one component only if they share at least k=2 models (at k=1 there would be 2 component(s)). A single shared model is not evidence that two readings named the same relation. Only models placed in `operations` are here: `unassigned` carries no words and `reversed` is excluded, so between 18% and 98% of what was sent reaches this graph depending on the rater.

nodes.label: explicit-to-neutral displacement
nodes.statement: The completion favored before tuning names a taboo body part or act outright, and the completion favored after tuning replaces it with an innocuous word from a different field entirely (grooming, generic anatomy, an animal, or a relative), never another taboo synonym.

nodes.label: in-register euphemism churn
nodes.statement: Both versions of the model stay inside the same taboo topic, and tuning only promotes a softer or blunter synonym for the same thing rather than changing the subject.

nodes.label: neutral-field reordering
nodes.statement: No candidate completion in either version touches the taboo topic at all; tuning merely reshuffles rank among members of one ordinary semantic field, such as grooming terms or kinship and pet terms.

nodes.label: explicit-to-decorous displacement
nodes.statement: Under the second condition, words that would complete the sentence in a taboo or transgressive way become rarer in the top ranks while ordinary, unremarkable completions of the same sentence become commoner.

nodes.label: same-register synonym churn
nodes.statement: Under both conditions the top-ranked completions are drawn from the same taboo or transgressive vocabulary, and only which particular synonym leads changes between conditions, with no ordinary alternative rising into the top ranks.

nodes.label: hair-surface convergence
nodes.statement: Under one condition the sentence's verb keeps an explicit, transgressive object; under the other, probability converges on one alternative object that is physically compatible with the same verb but carries no transgressive charge, typically something hair- or fur-covered, whether on the speaker's own body or an animal's.

nodes.label: generic-body diffusion
nodes.statement: Under one condition the verb keeps an explicit, transgressive object; under the other, probability spreads out across many ordinary non-erogenous nouns from the same broad category rather than converging on any single substitute.

nodes.label: relational recipient swap
nodes.statement: The possessive attached to the verb's object shifts from the speaker's own body to a named other person's, recasting a self-directed act as one performed on, or belonging to, someone else.

nodes.label: intra-register reweighting
nodes.statement: Both conditions keep the verb's object inside the same transgressive semantic field; only the leading word within that field changes, from a specific naming noun to a generic intensifier or a slang synonym for the same thing, so nothing exits the register.

nodes.label: Grooming retreat
nodes.statement: One condition favors an explicit anatomical completion where the other instead favors a self-directed grooming gesture toward the speaker's own face or hair.

nodes.label: Limb drift
nodes.statement: One condition favors an explicit anatomical completion where the other instead favors a generic, non-facial part of the speaker's own body, with no grooming or relational content added.

nodes.label: Redirect to another
nodes.statement: One condition favors an explicit anatomical completion where the other instead redirects the sentence's object onto a different being entirely, an animal companion or a named family member or partner.

nodes.label: Explicit vocabulary rotation
nodes.statement: Both conditions keep an explicit completion dominant, and what moves between them is only which explicit noun or intensifying modifier is favored, not whether the completion stays explicit.
